error_not_found: The requested item does not exist.
error_database_unavailable: The database is not reachable. Please try again later.
error_internal: Something went wrong on the server.
error_invalid_credentials: User name or password is wrong.
error_account_locked: This account is locked out. Try again later or ask an administrator.
error_password_change_required: The password must be changed first, for example when signing in to Windows.
error_too_many_attempts: Too many failed sign-ins. Please wait a few minutes.
error_forbidden_origin: The request came from another website and was blocked.
error_directory_unavailable: The directory (Active Directory) is not reachable.
vault_setup_hint: Choose a passphrase. Nobody can reset it for you: without the passphrase, a passkey or the recovery key, the entries are lost.
vault_recovery_hint: Write it down or print it, and keep it apart from the passphrase. It is shown only now.
vault_wrong: That does not unlock the vault.
vault_unreadable: This entry does not open with this vault's key.
vault_recovered_hint: An administrator recovered this vault. Keep this new recovery key, then choose a new passphrase.
vault_prf_unsupported: This passkey cannot derive keys (WebAuthn PRF). Use another one, e.g. a recent security key or your device's passkeys.
vault_reset_confirm: This deletes every entry and every way to unlock the vault. Nobody can bring them back.
audit_verify_ok: The log is intact: {entries} entries checked.
audit_verify_broken: The log was changed from entry {seq} on.
error_forbidden: You are not permitted to do this.
break_glass_intro: For when the directory is unavailable. Every sign-in here is recorded.
break_glass_banner: Signed in with an emergency account. Everything you do is recorded.
error_name_taken: This name is already used here.
error_folder_not_empty: Not empty. Move or delete what is in it first.
audit_device_keywords_changed: Changed the search words of a device
audit_device_moved: Moved a device to another folder
audit_credential_restored: Restored a credential from the recycle bin
audit_credential_code_shown: Showed or copied a one-time code
catalog_move_none: There is no folder you may move it into.
catalog_select_hint: Select a device or a folder.
field_password_keep: Leave empty to keep the current password.
auth_device_target_changed: Another target, or another kind, needs the password or key again.
auth_certificate: A certificate from remotehub, as myself
auth_laps_hint: Read from the directory at every connection.
auth_certificate_hint: remotehub signs a key for your user name, valid for minutes. The device's sshd must trust remotehub's certificate authority (TrustedUserCAKeys), whose public key is at {url}
requests_none_mine: You have not asked for access yet.
tree_drop_top_level: Drop here to move it to the top level
terminal_pinned: First connection: the host key {fingerprint} is now pinned.
terminal_credentials_hint: Used for this connection only and never stored.
terminal_host_key_changed: The host key of {name} changed: pinned {expected}, now {presented}. This happens when a device is reinstalled — or when someone intercepts the connection.
error_own_account_unavailable: Your sign-in password is not available in this session. Sign in again — or this is switched off here.
error_ssh_ca_unavailable: remotehub has no SSH certificate authority set up, so it cannot issue a certificate.
error_laps_unavailable: The directory holds no LAPS password for this device that remotehub may read.
error_last_unlock: The last way to unlock the vault cannot be removed.
error_vault_not_covered: This vault is not wrapped for the organisation recovery key yet. It will be at its next unlock.
error_recovery_key_in_use: Vaults still depend on this recovery key.
error_recovery_open: A recovery of this vault is open already.
error_recovery_not_ready: The recovery is not approved, or its day has passed.
error_request_pending: The same request is already waiting for a decision.
error_request_decided: This request has been decided already.
field_key_keep: Leave empty to keep the current key, passphrase and certificate.
error_field_private_key: This is not a private key in OpenSSH or PEM format.
error_field_passphrase: The key's passphrase is missing or wrong.
error_field_certificate: The certificate is not an OpenSSH user certificate for this key.
display_label: Remote desktop of {name} — click into it to type
display_failed_target: The device could not be reached, refused the sign-in or presented an unexpected certificate.
display_ended: The session was ended on the device.
credentials_username_optional: User name (if the device asks for one)
keyboard_layout_unicode: Unicode (any layout, some shortcuts may not work)
error_tls_required: The device offers Remote Desktop only without TLS; remotehub does not connect to it unencrypted.
audit_personal_unlock_added: Added a way to unlock the personal vault
audit_personal_unlock_removed: Removed a way to unlock the personal vault
display_certificate_pinned: First connection: the certificate {fingerprint} is now pinned.
display_certificate_changed: The certificate of {name} changed: pinned {expected}, now {presented}. This happens when a certificate is renewed — or when someone intercepts the connection.
connectors_token_hint: The connector's token. It is shown this once and kept nowhere.
connectors_token_docs: More in docs/install.md, section Reach devices in other networks.
connectors_setup_docker_hint: On a Linux host with Docker in the network of the devices. The second command waits for the token: paste it, then press Ctrl+D.
connectors_setup_windows_hint: Download both files to the Windows server. In a PowerShell as administrator, in their folder: both hashes must match, then the installer asks for the token.
connectors_setup_windows_served_hint: In a PowerShell as administrator on the Windows server: the commands download both files from remotehub into a folder of their own, stop if the hash does not match, and install the service; the installer asks for the token.
connectors_update_windows_served_hint: In a PowerShell as administrator on the Windows server: the commands download both files from remotehub, stop if the hash does not match, and the service takes this release. Token and settings stay.
connectors_download_hint: For a connector that exists: on another host, again, or in a new release. The commands ask for its token, the one shown when it was created.
connectors_update_docker_hint: On the host of the running connector. The container is replaced; the token file and the data volume stay.
connectors_update_windows_hint: Download both files to the Windows server, into a folder outside C:\Program Files. In a PowerShell as administrator, in that folder: both hashes must match, then the service takes the new release. Token and settings stay.
connectors_token_closed: Access starts closed. The customer opens it in the connector's web interface.
connector_access_partly: open in part: the customer opened single devices
device_access_open: open at the customer without end
ask_customer_hint: The request appears at the customer's connector with every address and port. A person there approves or refuses it.
access_intro: Who signs in, which groups and roles they hold, and what they reach.
access_read_only: You see this as an auditor and change nothing here.
access_directory_groups_note: Directory groups as read at the last sign-in. They change in the directory.
access_directory_members_note: Users as of their latest sign-in.
access_grant_hint: Pick one or more folders or devices. A grant on a folder holds for everything inside it.
access_grant_group_hint: A grant to a group holds for everyone in it, and is easier to keep up than many personal grants.
access_role_hint_reveal: Also shows stored passwords. Every reveal is audited.
access_ends_hint: The grant ends at the end of that day.
access_no_end_hint: The grant stays until someone removes it.
access_role_holders_note: As of each person's latest sign-in. The administrators set at installation are not listed.
access_pick_folder: Pick a folder to see who reaches it.
folder_connector_hint: For the devices in this folder and below it that take the folder's.
connector_closing: Access through {connector} ends at {time}. The customer closes it then.
error_connector_in_use: Devices or folders still use this connector.
error_retarget_forbidden: Devices below use login profiles you may not use, and would reach another target.
error_connector_offline: The device's connector is not connected.
error_connector_closed: The customer has closed access through the device's connector.
error_connector_target_closed: The customer has opened other devices at the connector, not this one.
error_connector_protocol: The connector speaks another protocol version than remotehub. Run the connector of remotehub's release.
error_purpose_required: State the purpose of the connection.
error_accounts_unavailable: The service for local accounts is not reachable.
error_second_factor_required: Confirm the sign-in with the second factor.
error_second_factor_setup_required: Set up a second factor first.
sign_in_use_key: Use a security key or passkey
passkey_failed: The passkey or security key did not answer, or the request was cancelled.
kratos_provider_not_linked: No account is linked to this sign-in. Sign in with the password once and link it under My account.
sign_in_second_hint: Enter the code from your authenticator app.
sign_in_recovery_hint: Enter one of your recovery codes. Each works once.
kratos_expired: This took too long. Please start again.
kratos_code_invalid: The code is not right. Please try again.
kratos_recovery_code_invalid: The code is not right, or was used already.
recovery_email_hint: Enter the address of your account. A code to set a new password goes there.
recovery_code_hint: Enter the code from your invitation or the e-mail.
setup_password_hint: Choose a password of at least 12 characters.
setup_totp_hint: remotehub asks for a second factor at every sign-in. Set up an authenticator app.
account_not_local: This account is managed in the directory.
account_totp_active: Set up. Every sign-in asks for its code.
account_totp_hint: Scan the code with an authenticator app, or enter the key by hand. Then enter the code the app shows.
account_totp_qr: QR code for the authenticator app
account_codes_hint: For when the authenticator app is not at hand. Each code works once.
account_passkeys_hint: A passkey signs you in instead of the password, with Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello or a security key. The second factor is still asked for.
account_keys_hint: A security key or passkey as the second factor, next to the authenticator app.
account_providers_hint: A linked account signs you in instead of the password. The second factor is still asked for.
audit_connector_opened: The customer opened access at a site connector
audit_connector_closed: The customer closed access at a site connector
audit_connector_access_requested: Asked the customer for access at a site connector
audit_connector_access_approved: The customer approved a request for access
audit_connector_access_refused: The customer refused a request for access
audit_connector_access_withdrawn: Withdrew a request to the customer
vault_unlock_to_use: Unlock my vault to use its entries
purpose_hint: It goes into the device's journal.
permissions_administrator: An administrator: reaches everything, without grants.
permissions_groups_last_sign_in: The directory did not answer: the groups are those of the last sign-in.
permissions_groups_unknown: The directory did not answer and there was no sign-in yet: groups of the directory are missing.
permissions_admins_reach_all: Administrators reach every folder as well.
permissions_nobody: No grants on this folder or above it.
recovery_intro: Personal vaults are also wrapped for the organisation recovery key. With its private key, an administrator can recover a vault once a security officer has approved it. The private key never reaches the server.
recovery_no_key: There is no recovery key yet. Without one, no personal vault can be recovered.
recovery_key_no_master: Holds no copy of the current master key; the server keeps one at its next start
recovery_key_create_hint: The private key is made in this browser. It is handed out twice: as a file sealed with this passphrase, and as text to print and keep in a safe. The server keeps only the public key.
recovery_key_shown_once: The key file was downloaded. Print this text and keep it in a safe. It is shown only now.
recovery_no_vaults: Nobody has set up a personal vault yet.
recovery_covered_older: Covered by an older key until the next unlock
recovery_not_covered: Not covered until the next unlock
recovery_kind_passphrase: Forgotten passphrase: a one-time recovery key for the owner
recovery_kind_handover: Hand-over: the entries go into a shared folder
recovery_key_unreadable: That is not a private key, or the passphrase is wrong.
recovery_key_wrong: This private key does not open the vault.
recovery_one_time_hint: Give this one-time recovery key to {name}. It unlocks the vault once; then a new passphrase and recovery key are due.
purpose_rules_hint: These users and groups state a purpose before every connection. It goes into the device's journal and the audit log.
users_block_confirm: Block {name}? Their sessions end now, and they cannot sign in until you unblock them.
users_end_sessions_confirm: End every session of {name}? They can sign in again.
users_recovery_confirm: Give {name} a new sign-in code? Their authenticator app stops working and their sessions end; with the code, they set a new password and second factor.
users_delete_confirm: Delete the account of {name}? This cannot be undone. The audit log keeps its entries.
users_invite_hint: Creates a local account. Hand its owner the link and the code; with them, they set a password and an authenticator app.
users_code_hint: Hand these to the account's owner. They are shown only now.
audit_account_recovery_issued: Issued a sign-in code for a local account
groups_hint: Groups of remotehub's own. Grant access to them like to directory groups; their members are users and directory groups.
groups_delete_confirm: Delete the group {name}? The permissions and purpose rules given to it go with it.
audit_group_member_added: Added a member to a group
audit_group_member_removed: Removed a member from a group
roles_hint: Roles for remotehub itself, given to users and groups. The administrators set at installation keep their role and are not listed here.
role_administrator_hint: Manages everything: devices, permissions, users and settings.
role_auditor_hint: Reads and checks the audit log.
audit_session_ended_by_directory: The directory ended a user's sessions
error_second_factor_invalid: The code is not right. Please try again.
factor_setup_required: Your account needs an authenticator app.
factor_setup_hint: Add it to your authenticator app with this key, then enter the code the app shows.
factor_none: Not set up. With an app, every sign-in asks for its code as well.
factor_required_here: Your account needs it: it stays.
factor_rules_hint: These users and groups set up an authenticator app at their next sign-in, and use it at every sign-in after. Local accounts always have one.
users_reset_factor_confirm: Remove the authenticator app of {name}, e.g. after a lost phone? If their account needs one, they set up a new one at the next sign-in.
audit_second_factor_waived: No longer asked for a second factor
reveal_copied: Copied. It leaves the clipboard in {seconds} seconds.
reveal_copy_failed: The browser did not let remotehub use the clipboard.
audit_credential_revealed: Showed or copied a stored credential
kdbx_new_password: Master password of the new file
kdbx_export_hint: The file holds every password in plain sight of whoever opens it with this master password. Keep it as safe as the vault.
kdbx_unreadable: The file does not open with this password, or it is no KeePass file.
kdbx_missing_reveal: An export takes the right to reveal everything in the folder, which {name} lacks.
vault_file_too_large: Files may have up to {megabytes} MB.
audit_credential_attachment_added: Added a file to a credential
audit_credential_attachment_deleted: Removed a file of a credential
audit_personal_attachment_saved: Saved a file of the personal vault
audit_personal_attachment_deleted: Deleted a file of the personal vault
error_setup_pending: remotehub is not set up yet.
error_setup_code_invalid: The setup link is not valid.
error_break_glass_exists: There is a break-glass account already.
error_last_administrator: The last administrator keeps the role.
wizard_waiting: remotehub is waiting for its setup. Open the link the installation printed, or make a new one on the server:
wizard_link_stale: This link does not work any more: remotehub is set up already, or a newer link replaced it. The server makes a new one:
wizard_command: sudo docker compose exec remotehub remotehub setup-code
wizard_administrator_hint: The first administrator is a local account. Next, it gets a password and an authenticator app.
wizard_sign_in: The administrator continues the setup after signing in.
wizard_not_yours: An administrator continues the setup, and this account is not one.
wizard_break_glass_hint: A break-glass account signs in when the directory or the service for local accounts is down. Print it and keep it offline, e.g. in a safe.
wizard_break_glass_exists: There is a break-glass account already.
wizard_break_glass_sheet_hint: Shown only this once. It signs in with the password and a code from an authenticator app that has this key.
wizard_skip_warning: Skip it anyway? Until someone makes up for it, administrators see a reminder.
wizard_recovery_key_hint: The organisation recovery key opens personal vaults whose owners forgot their passphrase, and it holds a copy of the master key. Its file is downloaded now; print its text too, and keep both apart from the server.
wizard_recovery_key_officer: A recovery needs the approval of a security officer other than whoever asks for it. Give the role to a second person under Users.
wizard_done_hint: remotehub is set up. Devices, folders and permissions come next.
wizard_hint_break_glass: There is no break-glass account. Create one on the server with remotehub break-glass create NAME.
wizard_hint_recovery_key: There is no organisation recovery key yet.
wizard_hint_certificate_root: remotehub has a certificate from its own CA. Browsers warn until its root certificate is on the clients.
wizard_directory_hint: Connect Active Directory, so that its users sign in with their own password. Without it, only local accounts sign in; it can be set later under Settings.
wizard_administrators_hint: Give a group of the directory the administrator role, so that its members administer remotehub too.
administrators_hint: Users and groups that administer remotehub. The last one keeps the role.
directory_hint: Active Directory over LDAPS, or LDAP with StartTLS. Its users sign in with their directory password.
directory_url_hint: ldaps://dc.example.com, or ldap:// with StartTLS under More settings.
directory_bind_dn_hint: It looks up users and groups, e.g. svc-remotehub@example.com.
directory_password_stored: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
directory_ca_hint: CA certificates, or the domain controller's own. Empty: the system's CAs decide.
directory_user_filter_hint: Only users that match this LDAP filter sign in, e.g. (memberOf=CN=remotehub users,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com).
directory_remove_confirm: Remove the connection? Directory users are signed out and cannot sign in until it is set again.
directory_saved: Saved; the next sign-in uses it.
directory_found: Connected: {count} users can sign in, e.g. {names}.
directory_found_more: Connected: more than {count} users can sign in, e.g. {names}.
directory_step_bind: signing in as the service account
directory_reason_refused: The server refuses connections on this port.
directory_reason_start_tls_refused: The server does not start TLS.
directory_reason_unknown_ca: The certificate comes from an unknown CA.
directory_reason_name_mismatch: The certificate is for another name.
directory_reason_no_such_base: The base DN does not exist.
directory_trust_ca_hint: Compare the fingerprint with the CA's before trusting it. Every certificate the CA signs for this name counts then.
directory_trust_server_hint: It is the domain controller's own certificate, sent without its CA. Compare the fingerprint before trusting it. It counts until the server gets a new one; the CA's certificate, added under More settings, covers every renewal.
error_directory_check_failed: The connection did not pass its check.
error_certificate_refused: The certificate does not fit this host.
error_caddy_refused: Caddy refused the certificate and keeps the one before.
error_caddy_unavailable: Caddy of the ops package is not reachable.
audit_tls_certificate_uploaded: Uploaded a certificate of its own
audit_tls_certificate_reset: Set the certificate back to automatic
wizard_mail_hint: With a mail server, invitations and the codes for a forgotten password go out by mail. Without one, administrators hand them over; it can be set later under Settings.
certificate_hint: The certificate Caddy serves remotehub with.
certificate_external: A reverse proxy of your own serves remotehub and holds its certificate.
certificate_source_lets_encrypt: From Let's Encrypt. Caddy renews it by itself.
certificate_source_remotehub: From remotehub's own CA. Browsers trust it once its root certificate is installed on the clients.
certificate_none: Caddy serves no certificate yet. It gets one when it starts, which can take a minute.
certificate_expired: It ran out on {date}. Browsers refuse it.
certificate_runs_out: It runs out on {date}. Upload its successor in time.
certificate_chain_incomplete: It came without the certificate that signed it, so some clients cannot check it. Upload it with its chain.
certificate_root_hint: Install it as a trusted root on every computer that opens remotehub, and browsers stop warning.
certificate_root_windows: Windows, for all computers of a domain: Group Policy, Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Public Key Policies > Trusted Root Certification Authorities, Import.
certificate_root_intune: Intune: a Trusted certificate profile with the .cer file, for Windows, macOS, iOS and Android.
certificate_root_mac: macOS: open the file, add it to the System keychain and set it to Always Trust.
certificate_root_linux: Linux: copy the .crt file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run update-ca-certificates.
certificate_upload_hint: From your company's CA or a public one, for {host}. Caddy serves it at once.
certificate_reset_confirm: Caddy then serves a certificate from Let's Encrypt or from its own CA again, and the stored certificate is deleted.
certificate_reset_done: Caddy gets its certificate automatically again.
certificate_refusal_unreadable: No certificate could be read from the file.
certificate_refusal_no_key: No private key could be read.
certificate_refusal_pfx_password: The PFX file does not open with this password.
certificate_refusal_key_mismatch: The key does not belong to the certificate.
certificate_refusal_unsupported_key: The key is neither RSA with at least 2048 bits nor ECDSA P-256 or P-384.
certificate_refusal_not_yet_valid: The certificate is not valid yet.
certificate_refusal_expired: The certificate has run out or runs out within a day.
mail_hint: remotehub mails invitations, new sign-in codes and the codes for a forgotten password through this server.
mail_security_none_hint: Only for a relay inside the network, usually on port 25. It takes no user name and no password.
mail_ca_hint: For a server whose certificate comes from a CA of your own. Empty: the system's CAs decide.
mail_remove_confirm: Remove the mail server? remotehub sends no mail then; administrators hand over invitations and codes.
mail_step_sign_in: The server refused the user name or the password.
mail_step_rejected: The server refused the mail. Its answer:
users_mailed: It went out by mail as well.
users_mail_failed: The mail did not go out. Hand over link and code yourself.
recovery_no_mail: remotehub sends no mail. An administrator gives out a new sign-in code, with a link of its own.
vault_locked_hint: Only you can open it: it is encrypted in your browser. Shared collections stay usable.
vault_locked_notice: Your personal vault is locked. Unlock it to see its entries here too.
vault_setup_notice: You have no personal vault yet. Set one up for entries only you see.
vault_collection_grants_hint: Access to a folder holds for every entry and folder in it.
profile_folder_hint: Devices in this folder and below may use it. Access follows the folder.
profile_used_by_hint: A new password holds for all of them at once.
profile_rights_hint: A login profile lies in a device folder and follows its access. Whoever may edit devices there assigns it; only who may reveal in that folder sees the password. Showing it is recorded.
profile_not_visible: A login profile you cannot see
device_keywords_hint: Everyone who sees this device may change them, and everyone's search finds it by them.
device_keywords_saved: Saved; the search finds it by them now.
device_secret_on_server: Stays on the server and is used there when connecting
error_profile_out_of_reach: A device may use only a login profile in its folder or one above. This change would leave devices without theirs.
error_profile_in_use: Devices still sign in with this login profile. Give them another sign-in first.
vault_password_keep: Leave it empty to keep the stored password.
vault_totp_hint: Paste the otpauth:// link of the QR code or the secret the service shows.
vault_totp_stored: Stored; leave empty to keep it
vault_totp_unreadable: This is no one-time password: expected an otpauth://totp link or a base32 secret.
vault_move_to_personal: Moves it into your personal vault: encrypted in your browser, and gone for everyone else.
vault_move_to_shared: Moves it into a shared folder: whoever has access there sees it.
vault_purge_confirm: Delete {title} for good? It cannot be restored.
vault_empty_bin_confirm: Delete {count} entries in the recycle bin for good? They cannot be restored.
vault_shortcuts_hint: Double-click copies user name or password · Enter edits · drag onto a folder to move
generator_hint: What the generator makes for everyone who keeps no default of their own.
generator_look_alikes: Also characters easily taken for others (0 O 1 l I)
generator_no_characters: Choose at least one kind of character.
viewer_failed: The file could not be opened.
viewer_none: This kind of file cannot be shown here. Download it to open it with another program.
viewer_truncated: Only the first {count} characters are shown.
viewer_download_hint: A downloaded file lies unencrypted on this computer.
error_extension_unknown: This browser extension may not connect to remotehub.
error_extension_outdated: The extension is older than this remotehub. Download it again from My account and reload it.
error_wrong_site: This page does not belong to the login.
extension_connect_hint: The remotehub extension in this browser asks to act for {user}.
extension_connect_lists: It lists the vault's logins that you may reveal.
extension_connect_fills: It fills a login into a web page when you ask it to, and only into pages the login belongs to.
extension_connect_audited: Every password it fills or copies goes into the audit log.
extension_connect_invalid: This link does not come from the remotehub extension. Start again in the extension.
account_extension_hint: Fills logins from the vault into web pages, in Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome and other Chromium browsers from version 127.
account_extension_step_unzip: Unzip it into a folder of its own in your profile, not onto a network share.
account_extension_step_developer: Open edge://extensions or chrome://extensions and turn on developer mode.
account_extension_step_load: Choose Load unpacked and select the folder.
account_extension_step_connect: Open the extension's settings and connect it to
account_extension_updates: An extension loaded unpacked does not update itself. After an update of remotehub, unzip the new version over the same folder and reload the extension.
account_extension_not_served: This installation of remotehub does not serve the extension.
account_extension_policy_hint: On PCs in an Active Directory domain, the policy ExtensionInstallForcelist installs the extension and its updates without developer mode. Its entry:
extension_description: Fills logins from your remotehub vault into web pages.
extension_command_fill: Fill the login of this page
extension_not_connected: The extension is not connected to remotehub yet.
extension_no_page: No web page is open in this tab.
extension_matches_none: No login belongs to this page.
extension_filled_user: User name filled in. The password follows on the next page.
extension_copied_secret: Copied. It leaves the clipboard in {seconds} seconds.
extension_search_hint: Logins of other pages can be copied, not filled in.
extension_shortcut: {keys} fills in the only login of a page.
extension_no_form: This page shows no sign-in form.
extension_no_code_field: This page shows no field for a one-time code.
extension_no_access: The extension may not read this page. Open it on the page itself.
extension_server_invalid: Enter the address with https://, as you open remotehub in the browser.
extension_permission_denied: Without access to remotehub's address, the extension cannot connect.
extension_connect_failed: Connecting did not work. Try again.
extension_unlock_hint: Your personal logins are end-to-end encrypted. Unlock them here with one of the ways you set up in remotehub.
extension_unlock_wrong: That did not unlock your personal logins.
extension_unlocked: Unlocked. Your personal logins show in the extension until the browser closes, you lock them, or they are not used for a while.
extension_no_personal: You have no personal logins yet. Set them up in remotehub's vault.
